lines.trans: Mei, wait—let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the top shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Qing, I just need the big teapot—ouch!
Mei! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair—don't stand up!
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes for me?
Toes move fine, nothing broken—just a sharp twist on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap cold ice in a clean towel.
No, no, Qing! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty lemon tarts to finish!
If you stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you won't walk for two weeks!
Who will bake Wednesday's fresh bread and lemon curd if I sit in a chair?!
Look around this house, Mei: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yí xià. Placed after an action verb to make a request or suggestion sound casual and brief (看一下, 等一下).

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng mian. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最上面 ('the very top').

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

examples.text: 上面有名字或者电话号码吗？
examples.trans: Is there a name or a phone number on it?

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià. Used for downward motion ('go down'), location ('under'), or 'next' (下周).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià lái. Compound directional complement for downward motion or writing something down to keep.

examples.text: 快问他叫什么名字！记下来！
examples.trans: Quick, ask him what his name is! Write it down!

examples.text: 请一定写下来！三楼热水：满分十分！
examples.trans: Please be sure to write that down! Third-floor hot water: ten out of ten!

meanings.note: Friendly farewell xiàcì jiàn.

examples.text: 今天聊得很开心，下次见！
examples.trans: Great chatting today, see you next time!

examples.text: 我们下次见！
examples.trans: See you next time!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià mian. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最下面 ('the bottom part').

examples.text: 快拿到楼下灯光下面看看吧！
examples.trans: Let's bring it downstairs under the light and take a look!

examples.text: 志豪先生早！在木房梁下面睡得好吗？
examples.trans: Morning, Mr Zhihao! Did you sleep well beneath the wooden beams?

examples.text: 这是不行啊。
examples.trans: This is cannot.

examples.text: 那个不行好。
examples.trans: That cannot is good.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Two tens: èrshí.

examples.text: 他二十岁了。
examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: 看了二十年电视。
examples.trans: Watched television for twenty years.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jīn wǎn. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 今天晚上 ('this evening').

examples.text: 今晚我应该能睡个好觉了。
examples.trans: Tonight I should be able to sleep well after all.

examples.text: 老陈……小晴……快告诉我今晚六号房空着。
examples.trans: Chen... Qing... please tell me room six is free tonight.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ. Everyday singular 'you' among colleagues, friends, and peers; use 您 for polite respect.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuò. Everyday verb for preparing food, doing work, or making objects.

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

examples.text: 小晴买了海盐黄油，今天我们做嫩炒蛋！
examples.trans: Qing bought sea-salt butter, so today we are making soft scrambled eggs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liù. Cardinal number 6.

examples.text: 老陈……小晴……快告诉我今晚六号房空着。
examples.trans: Chen... Qing... please tell me room six is free tonight.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bīng kuài. Combines 冰 ('ice') + 块 ('cube/chunk'); measure word: 块 (kuài) or 包 (bāo).

examples.text: 快把脚抬到椅子上放着，我去用干净毛巾包点冰块敷一下。
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the chair while I go wrap some ice cubes in a clean towel for it.

examples.text: 夏天喝柠檬薄荷水的时候，加两块冰块最解暑。
examples.trans: When drinking lemon mint water in summer, adding two ice cubes is the most refreshing.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng rǔ. Combines 凝 ('congeal/set into a smooth custard') + 乳 ('milk/creamy emulsion'); 柠檬凝乳 is the culinary term for lemon curd.

examples.text: 要是我坐在椅子上休息，明天早上的柠檬凝乳谁来熬呢？
examples.trans: If I sit resting in a chair, who will cook tomorrow morning's lemon curd?

examples.text: 用新鲜蛋黄和柠檬汁慢火熬出的柠檬凝乳又香又滑。
examples.trans: Lemon curd cooked slowly over low heat with fresh egg yolks and lemon juice is fragrant and silky.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bié. Most commonly means 'do not' in polite commands (别担心 'don't worry'); as a verb, 'pin/clip on'.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

副.gloss: measure word for glasses, sets, expressions

meanings.en: measure word for glasses, sets, expressions
meanings.note: Pinyin: fù. Counts eyeglasses, gloves, chess sets, and facial expressions (一副眼镜 'a pair of glasses').

examples.text: 法律条文我戴两副眼镜看都头疼！
examples.trans: Legal clauses give me a headache even with two pairs of glasses!

examples.text: 桌子上放着一副旧眼镜。
examples.trans: A pair of old glasses is sitting on the table.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dòng. Used for physical movement (别动 'don't move!').

examples.text: 全都别动！现在几点？九点三十五分！
examples.trans: Hold everything! What time is it right now? Nine thirty-five!

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dòng dong. Tentative reduplication of 动 ('move'); second syllable takes neutral tone.

examples.text: 小晴轻轻帮小美脱下鞋子说：“你能动动脚趾给我看看吗？”
examples.trans: Gently slipping off Mei's shoe, Qing asked, 'Can you wiggle your toes for me to see?'

examples.text: 在钢琴前坐久了，站起来动动肩膀和手指会舒服很多。
examples.trans: After sitting at the piano for a long time, standing up to stretch your shoulders and fingers feels much better.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bāo. As a verb, 'wrap up' (白纸包着); as a noun/classifier, 'bag/packet'.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

examples.text: 等一下，小晴……你拿了哪一包黄油？
examples.trans: Wait a second, Qing... which packet of butter did you grab?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí. Cardinal number 10; building block for 11–99.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qù. Movement away from the speaker, as main verb (去车站) or directional complement (上去).

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuāng. Counts naturally paired items: shoes, socks, chopsticks, hands (一双皮鞋 'a pair of leather shoes').

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

examples.text: 天哪……看这双眼睛！第三级台阶上的小志豪？！
examples.trans: Good heavens... look at those eyes! Little Zhihao from the third step?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu jiǎo. Combines 右 ('right') + 脚 ('foot'); contrasts with 左脚 ('left foot'); measure word: 只 (zhī).

examples.text: 我从矮凳往下迈的时候，右脚鞋子在横档上滑了一下。
examples.trans: When I stepped down from the low stool, my right shoe slipped on the rung.

examples.text: 弹钢琴到柔和的乐段时，宋老师轻轻踩下了右脚的延音踏板。
examples.trans: Reaching the gentle passage on the piano, Teacher Song lightly pressed the sustain pedal with her right foot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ma. Placed at the end of any statement to turn it into a neutral yes/no question.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: ya. Gentle exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 呀，这就是星期一火车上那只双胞胎箱子吗？
examples.trans: Oh, is this that twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: ne. After a noun, asks 'what about X?' (你呢？); at the end of a statement, highlights an ongoing situation.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: āi yō. Natural spoken exclamation of effort, surprise, or mild pain.

examples.text: 哎哟，这扇旧木窗板卡得真紧呀！
examples.trans: Ugh, this old wooden shutter is stuck so tight!

examples.text: 哎哟，茶杯还很烫，端的时候小心点儿。
examples.trans: Ooh, the teacup is still very hot—be careful carrying it.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sǎng mén. Colloquial compound 嗓 ('throat/voice') + 门 ('gate/opening'); measure word: 副 (fù); 大嗓门 means a booming, carrying voice.

examples.text: 小美，在这栋房子里你有六双手帮忙，还有一副大嗓门呢！
examples.trans: Mei, in this house you have six pairs of helping hands and one booming voice!

examples.text: 隔着整个院子都能听见老陈爽朗的大嗓门。
examples.trans: You can hear Chen's hearty, booming voice all the way across the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sī. Onomatopoeic interjection imitating a sharp intake of breath through the teeth when feeling sudden pain or cold.

examples.text: 嘶……我往下迈的时候，右脚踝不小心扭了一下！
examples.trans: Ooh... when I stepped down, I twisted my right ankle!

examples.text: 刚出炉的烤盘真烫，志鹏不小心碰到边缘，嘶地倒吸了一口冷气。
examples.trans: The baking tray fresh from the oven was so hot that Peng gasped sharply when he brushed the edge.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuò. Means both 'sit down' (请坐) and 'ride inside a vehicle' (坐火车 'take the train').

examples.text: 是的，宋老师，二楼四号房！坐火车累吗？
examples.trans: Yes, Teacher Song, room four on the second floor! Was the train ride tiring?

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wài cè. Place noun 外 ('outer') + 侧 ('side/flank'); contrasts with 内侧 ('inner side').

examples.text: 我的骨头没事，就是右脚踝外侧稍微扭了一下。
examples.trans: My bones are fine—I just twisted the outer side of my right ankle slightly.

examples.text: 老陈在绿窗板的外侧又仔细刷了第二遍防水油漆。
examples.trans: Chen carefully brushed a second coat of weatherproof paint onto the outer side of the green shutters.

meanings.note: adverb

examples.text: 职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
examples.trans: The workplace is a hotpot; just thinking about it is scary enough.

examples.text: 职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
examples.trans: The workplace is a hotpot; just thinking about it is scary enough.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà. Everyday adjective for size, age, and strong wind or rain.

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà jiā. Warm collective pronoun including everyone in the group.

examples.text: 大家早上好！欢迎你，小晴。都准备好了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Qing. Is everything ready?

examples.text: 有进步！今天小院迎接兄弟重逢——大家保持安静端庄！
examples.trans: Progress! Today our courtyard hosts a brotherly reunion—quiet dignity from everyone!

meanings.note: Pinyin: háo hǎo. Placed before a verb to urge doing it well (好好看看, 好好休息).

examples.text: 您好好休息，有事随时按铃。
examples.trans: Rest well, ma'am; ring the bell anytime if you need anything.

examples.text: 把电话给我，我来好好问他！
examples.trans: Hand me the phone; let me ask him properly!

meanings.note: Pinyin: wán. Most often follows an action verb as a result complement meaning 'finish doing' (读完, 弹完).

examples.text: 每次弹完琴，他都问为什么下雨天钢琴声音更暖。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer on rainy days.

examples.text: 十二下敲完了……大门外面街上空荡荡的。
examples.trans: Twelve chimes have finished... and the street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo. Everyday adjective for small size; also prefixes younger colleagues' names warmly (小晴, 小美).

examples.text: 早上好，姑娘。我有一个宋名下的预订。
examples.trans: Good morning, young lady. I have a booking for Song.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Highlights immediacy, exact location (就在这里), or smooth consequence ('then').

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù shì. Adds emphatic certainty before a noun ('is the very one').

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 没关系！您就是志豪先生吧？
examples.trans: No problem at all! You must be Mr Zhihao, right?

层.gloss: measure word for floors and layers

meanings.en: measure word for floors and layers
meanings.note: Pinyin: céng. Counts building stories (三层 'third floor') and coatings/layers (一层糖粉 'a layer of powdered sugar').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 面包上面撒了一层白糖粉。
examples.trans: A thin layer of powdered sugar is dusted over the bread.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gān jìng. Note first tone gān ('dry/clean'), never fourth tone.

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

examples.text: 放心吧，周经理。房间干净，毛巾也是新的。
examples.trans: Relax, Manager Zhou. The room is clean, and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: 干活累。
examples.trans: Working is tiring.

examples.text: 努力干活。
examples.trans: Work hard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng. Guides movement in directions (往上提 'lift upward', 往左拐 'turn left').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Read de after a verb to introduce how it goes (走得快 'walk fast'); read děi before a verb to mean 'must'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.en: want to; would like to; think; miss
meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎng. Before a verb, expresses a polite wish ('would like to'); before a noun/person, 'think of / miss'.

examples.text: 太好了！现在我想吃一顿丰盛的早餐。
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I would like to eat a big breakfast.

examples.text: 宋老师早！您想喝咖啡还是红茶？
examples.trans: Morning, Teacher Song! Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fáng zi. Measure word (量词): 栋 (dòng), e.g. 一栋房子 ('a house').

examples.text: 所以老房子自己会打招呼？
examples.trans: So the old house says hello by itself?

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

meanings.note: Pinyin: biǎn dòu. Literally 扁 ('flat') + 豆 ('bean/legume'), used for flat-podded beans and lentils.

examples.text: 加了柠檬和橄榄油的金黄扁豆汤又香又暖胃。
examples.trans: Golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil is fragrant and warming.

examples.text: 小美前一天晚上先把扁豆洗干净泡好。
examples.trans: Mei washed and soaked the lentils the night before.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shǒu. Measure word (量词): 双 (shuāng), e.g. 一双手 ('a pair of hands').

examples.text: 谢谢你，小美。刚才吓了一跳，手都凉了！
examples.trans: Thank you, Mei. That gave me such a start just now that my hands went cold!

examples.text: 我手在发抖——车上下来穿深灰色外套的高个子男人吗？
examples.trans: My hands are shaking—is a tall man in a dark grey coat stepping out?

related.gloss: a pair of hands (measure word 双)

meanings.note: Pinyin: niǔ. Action verb for twisting or spraining a joint (扭了脚踝 'twisted an ankle') or turning a knob.

examples.text: 我的骨头没事，就是下木凳的时候右脚踝外侧扭了一下。
examples.trans: My bones are fine—I just twisted the outside of my right ankle slightly stepping off the wooden stool.

examples.text: 搬重木桌的时候要注意脚下，小心别扭了腰或脚踝。
examples.trans: Watch your step when carrying heavy wooden tables so you don't twist your back or ankle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fú zhù. Resultative verb compound 扶 ('support with the hand') + 住 ('firmly in place').

examples.text: 小美，你够最上面那层架子的时候，让我先扶住那个木凳！
examples.trans: Mei, let me hold that wooden stool steady while you reach for the top shelf!

examples.text: 志豪在下面稳稳扶住木梯子，让老陈安心挂好上面的窗板。
examples.trans: Hao held the wooden ladder steady from below so Chen could hang the upper shutter safely.

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuā zhù. Resultative compound 抓 ('grab') + 住 ('hold fast').

examples.text: 小晴稳稳抓住了第一扇木窗板的左头。
examples.trans: Qing grabbed firm hold of the left end of the first wooden shutter.

examples.text: 下梯子的时候请双手抓住两边的扶手。
examples.trans: When coming down the ladder, please hold tightly onto both side rails.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tái. Means raising upward or two people lifting an object together.

examples.text: 我们俩一起把这扇长窗板抬进走廊吧。
examples.trans: Let's lift this tall shutter together and carry it into the hallway.

examples.text: 按下琴键时，里面的小琴槌就会稳稳抬起来。
examples.trans: When you press the piano key, the small hammer inside rises smoothly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ná. Core verb for holding or fetching objects in the hand.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 火车站有人拿错了我的蓝色行李箱！
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.note: Verb/noun zhǐhuī ('command, direct').

examples.text: 今晚您还是待在中控室里进行指挥吧。
examples.trans: Tonight you should stay in the control room to direct.

examples.text: 导演在现场指挥摄像。
examples.trans: The director commands the cameras on set.

meanings.note: Pinyin: fàng. Everyday verb for placing an object somewhere (放在桌子上).

examples.text: 我们不知道。有人放在台阶上，按了门铃。
examples.trans: We do not know. Someone set it on the step and rang the bell.

examples.text: 小勺子和餐巾放在哪里？
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīn xiān. Describes fresh fruit, fresh juice, or fresh herbs.

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 明天一天 ('all day tomorrow').

examples.text: 欢迎来到小院客栈，小晴。明天不会无聊了。
examples.trans: Welcome to Courtyard Inn, Qing. Tomorrow will not be boring.

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个星期 ('a week').

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 脑子转得快，小晴。志豪每星期都读城市建筑规定。
examples.trans: Quick thinking, Qing. Hao reads city building rules every single week.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī sān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 这星期三 ('this Wednesday').

examples.text: 等等——星期三晚上你又用真名住进来了？
examples.trans: Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?

examples.text: 每到星期三下午，小美都会试烤新甜点。
examples.trans: Every Wednesday afternoon, Mei test-bakes a new pastry.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuì. Superlative adverb placed before adjectives or feeling verbs (最好 'best', 最喜欢 'like best').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 最上面架子上金色包装那包。怎么了？
examples.trans: The gold-wrapped packet on the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǒu. Expresses both possession ('I have') and existence ('there is'); ALWAYS negated with 没 (没有), never 不.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

meanings.note: Pinyin: mù dèng. Combines 木 ('wood/wooden') + 凳 ('stool/bench without a backrest'); measure word: 把 (bǎ) or 张 (zhāng).

examples.text: 小美，你踩着木凳够最上面那层架子的时候，让我扶住它！
examples.trans: Mei, let me hold that wooden stool steady while you stand on it to reach the top shelf!

examples.text: 老陈在工具间里做了一把结实的小木凳。
examples.trans: Chen built a sturdy little wooden stool in the workshop.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lái. Movement toward the speaker, as main verb or directional complement (进来 'come in').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jià zi. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个架子 ('a shelf').

examples.text: 最上面架子上金色包装那包。怎么了？
examples.trans: The gold-wrapped packet on the top shelf. Why?

examples.text: 他拿旧阀门比对了——架子上正好还剩两个！
examples.trans: He matched it against the old valve—he has two left on the shelf!

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个柠檬 ('a lemon').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng tà. Combines 柠檬 ('lemon') + 挞 ('tart', phonetic loan from English 'tart').

examples.text: 星期二我们要修好琴键，还要烤星期三的柠檬挞！
examples.trans: On Tuesday we will fix the piano key and bake Wednesday's lemon tarts!

examples.text: 酸甜清香的杏仁柠檬挞成了咖啡角的招牌甜点。
examples.trans: Sweet-tart, fragrant almond lemon tart became the café corner's signature dessert.

栋.gloss: measure word for buildings and houses

meanings.en: measure word for buildings and houses
meanings.note: Pinyin: dòng. Counts whole standalone buildings (一栋老房子 'an old building').

examples.text: 二十五年前？就在同一栋房子里？
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago? Right inside that very same house?

examples.text: 产权转让通知：八号小院整栋建筑将作为商业办公楼出售。
examples.trans: Property Transfer Notice: Courtyard Building Eight offered for sale as commercial offices.

根.gloss: measure word for pipes, wires, sticks

meanings.en: measure word for pipes, wires, sticks
meanings.note: Pinyin: gēn. Counts long, thin rod-like or cord-like objects (一根水管 'a water pipe', 一根电线 'a wire').

examples.text: 先生，到了。小心碰头，这根木房梁比较低。
examples.trans: Here we are, sir. Mind your head—this wooden beam is fairly low.

examples.text: 老木匠换了一根新的铜水管。
examples.trans: The carpenter replaced it with a new copper water pipe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ zi. Measure word (量词): 把 (bǎ), e.g. 一把椅子 ('a chair').

examples.text: 四张桌子，八把椅子，全摆好了！
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs—everything is set in place!

examples.text: 当心那把角落椅子，等十秒我拧紧螺丝。
examples.trans: Mind that corner chair—wait ten seconds while I tighten the screw.

meanings.note: Pinyin: héng dāng. Combines 横 ('horizontal') + 档 ('crosspiece/rung of a ladder, stool, or chair'); measure word: 根 (gēn).

examples.text: 小美往下迈的时候，右脚鞋子在矮凳最下面那根横档上滑了一下。
examples.trans: When Mei stepped down, her right shoe slipped on the bottom rung of the low stool.

examples.text: 老陈检查了木椅子的四条腿和底下的每一根横档，确保稳固安全。
examples.trans: Chen checked all four legs and every bottom rung of the wooden chairs to make sure they were solid and safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cì. Standard verbal measure word counting how many times an action happens (一次 'once', 下次 'next time').

examples.text: 每次弹完琴，他都问为什么下雨天钢琴声音更暖。
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer on rainy days.

examples.text: 说这话的人每隔三十秒就扒着窗帘偷看一次！
examples.trans: Says the man peeking through the window curtain every thirty seconds!

meanings.note: Pinyin: máo jīn. Measure word (量词): 条 (tiáo), e.g. 一条毛巾 ('a towel').

examples.text: 放心吧，周经理。房间干净，毛巾也是新的。
examples.trans: Relax, Manager Zhou. The room is clean, and the towels are fresh.

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tāng. Measure word (量词): 碗 (wǎn), e.g. 一碗汤 ('a bowl of soup').

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

examples.text: 热汤？在冷雨中走过来之后，这听起来太棒了。
examples.trans: Hot soup? After that cold walk in the rain, that sounds wonderful.

related.gloss: a bowl of soup (measure word 碗)

meanings.note: everyday phrase meaning unhurt or 'it is nothing'

examples.text: 您没事吧？我是布小谷。
examples.trans: Are you alright? I am Bu Xiaogu.

examples.text: 我没事，休息一会儿就好了。
examples.trans: I am fine; I will be alright after resting a bit.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huá. Describes wet stone steps being slippery or an object sliding down.

examples.text: 周经理！这回您眼镜从鼻子上滑下来是因为太高兴啦！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou! This time your glasses slid off your nose from sheer joy!

examples.text: 听我把箱子斜过来——里面有金属东西滑了一下。
examples.trans: Listen as I tilt the box—something metal slid inside.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diǎn. Marks hours on the clock (八点 'eight o'clock') or 'a bit' (一点).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kǎo. Used for baking bread, rolls, and cakes in an oven.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 多烤几块边角，好姑娘！
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, dear girl!

meanings.note: Pinyin: pá. Used for climbing stairs, hills, or ladders.

examples.text: 真的？您不介意多爬几步楼梯？
examples.trans: Really? You do not mind climbing a few extra stairs?

examples.text: 何止认识！整整六年，每个星期五我都爬那座木楼梯教钢琴！
examples.trans: More than know it! Every Friday for six whole years I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòng. Works as main verb ('use a key') or preposition ('with/using').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: de shí hou. High-frequency temporal frame placed at the end of a verb or clause to mean 'when / while ...' (往下迈的时候 'when stepping down').

examples.text: 小美够最上面那层架子的时候，小晴赶紧上前扶住了木凳。
examples.trans: While Mei was reaching for the top shelf, Qing hurried over to steady the wooden stool.

examples.text: 我擦厨房台面的时候，罐子底下的纸标签不小心被水弄湿了。
examples.trans: When I was wiping the kitchen counter, the paper labels under the jars got damp.

meanings.en: take a look; have a quick look
meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn kan. Friendly reduplicated form of 看.

examples.text: 快拿到楼下灯光下面看看吧！
examples.trans: Let's bring it downstairs under the light and take a look!

examples.text: 哎呀，怎么拿错了！我戴眼镜看看行李牌。
examples.trans: Dear me, what a mix-up! Let me put on my glasses and check the luggage tag.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ǎi dèng. Combines 矮 ('low/short in height') + 凳 ('stool'); measure word: 把 (bǎ) or 张 (zhāng).

examples.text: 小美笑着说：“这把小矮凳我一星期爬十次，拿个茶壶很快的！”
examples.trans: Mei laughed, 'I climb this little low stool ten times a week—grabbing the teapot will only take a second!'

examples.text: 擦窗框底下的时候，坐在小矮凳上干活最省力。
examples.trans: When wiping the lower window frames, sitting on a low stool saves the most effort.

meanings.note: Adjective/adverb yìng ('by sheer force, despite pain').

examples.text: 老大，你胃不好还这样硬喝不要命了吗？
examples.trans: Boss, forcing down drinks with a bad stomach risks your life!

examples.text: 虽然发着低烧，他还是硬撑着录完了全场。
examples.trans: Despite a fever, he toughed it out through the taping.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhàn. As a verb, 'stand' (站在旁边); as a noun, 'station/stop' (火车站).

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

examples.text: 听得很清楚。你站在小石头喷泉旁边吗？
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you standing beside the little stone fountain?

examples.text: 这是第二啊。
examples.trans: This is second.

examples.text: 那个第二好。
examples.trans: That second is good.

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng deng. Urgent or casual reduplication of 等 ('wait!').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gěi. As main verb, 'give'; as preposition/complement, marks the recipient (给你 'for/to you', 递给我 'pass to me').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǒng. Used both as an inchoative verb (肿起来 'swell up') and stative adjective; contrasts with 消肿 ('go down in swelling').

examples.text: 今晚你要是硬站在肿起来的脚踝上，接下来两星期都走不了路！
examples.trans: If you stubbornly stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you won't be able to walk for the next two weeks!

examples.text: 敷上冰块休息了一晚，小美扭伤的脚踝没有继续肿起来。
examples.trans: After icing it and resting all night, Mei's sprained ankle did not swell up any further.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gē bo. Everyday spoken noun for the arm (shoulder to wrist); second syllable is neutral tone.

examples.text: 那本绿色的旧登记本不就夹在你胳膊底下吗？
examples.trans: Isn't that old green guest book tucked right under your arm?

examples.text: 抬了四扇厚木窗板，我的两条胳膊都有点酸了。
examples.trans: After carrying four thick wooden shutters, both my arms are a bit sore.

meanings.note: Pinyin: néng. Expresses practical ability or whether circumstances allow something (能睡个好觉).

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

examples.text: 今晚我应该能睡个好觉了。
examples.trans: Tonight I should be able to sleep well after all.

meanings.note: Lower extremity of the leg.

examples.text: 蹲了太久，我的脚都有点麻了。
examples.trans: After squatting so long, my foot went a bit numb.

examples.text: 走了一整天路，脚特别酸。
examples.trans: After walking all day, my feet are really sore.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo zhǐ. Combines 脚 ('foot') + 趾 ('toe/digit of the foot'); measure word: 个 (gè) or 根 (gēn).

examples.text: 小美动了动脚趾说：“脚趾动得好好的，骨头一点没事！”
examples.trans: Mei wiggled her toes and said, 'My toes move just fine—nothing broken at all!'

examples.text: 冬天穿上一双厚羊毛袜，连脚趾头都是暖乎乎的。
examples.trans: Put on a pair of thick wool socks in winter and even your toes stay toasty warm.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo huái. Combines 脚 ('foot') + 踝 ('ankle joint'); measure word: 只 (zhī) or 个 (gè).

examples.text: 志鹏关心地问：“小美，今天早上你的脚踝感觉怎么样？”
examples.trans: Peng asked warmly, 'Mei, how does your ankle feel this morning?'

examples.text: 休息了一天半以后，小美扭伤的脚踝已经消肿，到星期五就能站起来了。
examples.trans: After a day and a half of rest, Mei's sprained ankle has gone down in swelling and she will be able to stand by Friday.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tuō. Opposite of 穿; often pairs with 掉 (脱掉 'take off').

examples.text: 坐下吧，志鹏，脱掉厚外套，看看这个蓝色行李箱。
examples.trans: Sit down, Zhipeng, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.

examples.text: 进屋很暖和，把厚外套脱掉吧。
examples.trans: It is warm inside—take off your heavy coat.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá hú. Measure word (量词): 把 (bǎ), e.g. 一把茶壶 ('a teapot').

examples.text: 小晴，把热水倒进茶壶里，他们来了！
examples.trans: Qing, pour the hot water into the teapot—here they come!

examples.text: 茶壶也烫好了！大家从窗边退后一步！
examples.trans: And the teapot is hot! Everybody step back from the window!

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yào shi. Everyday spoken 'if', often paired with 就 in the main clause.

examples.text: 等等——要是每天早上打开院门，卖街坊咖啡和热面包……
examples.trans: Wait—if we open our courtyard gate every morning for neighbourhood coffee and warm bread...

examples.text: 周经理，要是你不正式聘用她，我就请她进我厨房！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou, if you do not hire her permanently, I am hiring her into my kitchen!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ràng. Everyday causative/polite-offer verb (让我看看 'let me have a look').

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 宋老师，让我来给您倒新鲜橙汁！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, allow me to pour fresh orange juice for you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuí. Question pronoun for people; stays in the exact spot of the answer (这是谁的？ 'Whose is this?').

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 一点没破！是谁送回来的？
examples.trans: Not cracked at all! Who brought it back?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǒu bu liǎo lù. Potential complement phrase 走 ('walk') + 不了 (bu liǎo, 'unable to') + object 路 ('road/steps').

examples.text: 今晚你要是硬站在肿起来的脚踝上，接下来两星期都走不了路！
examples.trans: If you stubbornly stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you won't be able to walk for two weeks!

examples.text: 提着这么重的两桶水，谁都走不了快路。
examples.trans: Carrying two buckets of water this heavy, nobody can walk fast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qǐ lái. Marks standing up or beginning/evaluating an action.

examples.text: 摸摸铜管！已经热起来了！
examples.trans: Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!

examples.text: 快把那张纸折起来，塞进口袋里。
examples.trans: Fold up that sheet of paper right now and tuck it into your pocket.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ruǎn diàn. Combines 软 ('soft') + 垫 ('cushion/pad'); measure word: 个 (gè) or 块 (kuài).

examples.text: 小美哭笑不得地说：“你是想让我坐在软垫上指挥大家干活？！”
examples.trans: Mei laughed half in disbelief: 'You want me to sit on a soft cushion and direct everyone at work?!'

examples.text: 木椅子上加了一块厚实的亚麻软垫，坐一整个下午也不累。
examples.trans: With a thick linen cushion added to the wooden chair, you can sit all afternoon in comfort.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng qīng. Reduplication of 轻 ('light/soft'), used directly before short verbs or with 地 (轻轻地抽出来).

examples.text: 宋老师用两根手指把旧乐谱轻轻抽了出来。
examples.trans: Teacher Song gently slid the old music sheet out with two fingers.

examples.text: 怕吵醒午睡的客人，小晴轻轻关上了木门。
examples.trans: So as not to wake guests napping at noon, Qing closed the wooden door softly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: mài. Action verb for lifting one's foot and stepping forward or down (往下迈 'step down', 迈进大门 'step through the gate').

examples.text: 我从矮凳往下迈的时候，右脚鞋子在最下面那根横档上滑了一下。
examples.trans: When I stepped down from the low stool, my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung.

examples.text: 周经理整理好领带，微笑着迈出大门去迎接市政厅的办事员。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou straightened his tie and stepped out the front gate with a smile to greet the City Hall clerk.

meanings.en: and also; in addition; still have
meanings.note: Pinyin: hái yǒu. Adds another item to a list ('plus…').

examples.text: 只有裙子、乐谱，还有我最喜欢的茶杯！
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite teacup!

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè. Proximal demonstrative; pairs with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: tóng. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块铜 ('a piece of brass').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 楼下我的工具房里有一盏铜台灯。
examples.trans: Downstairs in my workshop there is a brass desk lamp.

related.gloss: a piece of brass (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: miàn bāo. Measure word (量词): 片 (piàn), e.g. 一片面包 ('a slice of bread').

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 闻闻看！热面包、热炒蛋，还有新鲜香草。
examples.trans: Smell that! Warm bread, hot scrambled eggs, and fresh herbs.

related.gloss: a slice of bread (measure word 片)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xié. Measure word (量词): 双 (shuāng), e.g. 一双鞋 ('a pair of shoes').

examples.text: 我可不穿四十四码的鞋！
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four shoes!

examples.text: 为什么把鞋和木头小火车留到星期五呢？
examples.trans: Why leave the shoes and little wooden train here until Friday?

related.gloss: a pair of shoes (measure word 双)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xié zi. Combines 鞋 ('shoe') + noun suffix 子; measure word: 双 (shuāng, pair) or 只 (zhī, single); verbs: 穿 ('put on/wear'), 脱 ('take off').

examples.text: 我从矮凳往下迈的时候，右脚鞋子在横档上滑了一下。
examples.trans: When I stepped down from the low stool, my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung.

examples.text: 进屋以前，大家都在门口的垫子上把鞋子底下的雨水擦干。
examples.trans: Before stepping indoors, everyone wiped the rainwater off the soles of their shoes on the doormat.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gǔ tou. Combines 骨 ('bone') + nominal suffix 头 (neutral tone); measure word: 根 (gēn) or 块 (kuài).

examples.text: 小美动了动脚趾，放心地说：“骨头没事，只是脚踝扭了一下。”
examples.trans: Mei wiggled her toes and said with relief, 'The bones are fine—I just twisted my ankle slightly.'

examples.text: 用牛骨头和新鲜蔬菜慢火熬出来的高汤味道特别浓郁。
examples.trans: Stock simmered slowly from beef bones and fresh vegetables has an especially rich flavour.
